caption: The longest dive ever recorded for any mammal belongs to a Cuvier's beaked whale: 222 minutes, or 3 hours and 42 minutes on a single breath (Guinness World Records, 2020). Most people can't hold their breath for more than a minute or two. Whales manage it because their muscles are packed with myoglobin, a protein that stores oxygen, and their heart rate slows dramatically during deep dives to make that oxygen last. There's a catch, though. Whales don't breathe automatically like we do. Every breath is a conscious decision, which is why dolphins and many whales rest only half their brain at a time. Imagine having to remember every single breath. How long can YOU hold yours? Try it on land only, never underwater. 👇
